title: Singapore water supply: plan to 2061
caption: The 1962 Johor water agreement ends in 2061; Singapore's own sources must cover demand by then.
summary: Singapore turns used water and seawater into most of its supply, so by 2060 recycled and desalinated water can meet up to 85% of needs.

nodes.label: PUB
nodes.detail:
The national water agency.
It plans, builds and runs every tap.

nodes.label: Water price
nodes.detail: Up 20 cents a cubic metre in April 2024 and 30 more in April 2025, so each litre carries its real cost.

nodes.label: Rain catchment
nodes.detail: About two-thirds of the land drains into reservoirs, through more than 8,000 km of drains and canals.

nodes.label: Johor River (imported)
nodes.detail: The 1962 agreement lets Singapore draw up to 250 million gallons a day, at 3 sen per 1,000 gallons.

risks.label: Agreement ends in 2061
risks.detail: After that, the island's own taps must carry the load.

nodes.label: Seawater
nodes.detail: Unlimited supply; desalination uses the most energy of the four sources.

nodes.label: Used water
nodes.detail: Used water from homes and industry is collected and reclaimed, not discharged.

nodes.label: PUB water system
nodes.detail: Collects, treats, supplies and reclaims water across all four sources.

nodes.label: Deep Tunnel Sewerage System
nodes.detail:
Carry used water by gravity to the reclamation plants.
Phase 2 was about 80% complete at the end of November 2025.

nodes.label: NEWater factories
nodes.detail:
Four factories clean reclaimed water until it is ultra-pure.
Up to 55% of needs by 2060.

nodes.label: Desalination plants
nodes.detail:
Five plants today, a sixth being studied.
Up to 30% of needs by 2060.

nodes.label: Reservoirs and waterworks
nodes.detail: Hold rain and imported water, then treat it to drinking standard.

nodes.label: Households
nodes.detail:
About 45% of today's demand.
141 litres a person a day in 2023.

nodes.label: Industry, including wafer fabs
nodes.detail:
About 55% of demand today, more than 60% by 2065.
Fabs are NEWater's biggest users.

nodes.label: Johor (treated water sold back)
nodes.detail: Singapore usually sells back 16 million gallons of treated water a day, at 50 sen per 1,000 gallons.

nodes.label: Drinking-water tests
nodes.detail: Samples are tested against Singapore's drinking-water rules, which follow WHO guidelines.

edges.label: Plans, builds and operates
edges.detail: One agency owns the whole loop, from drain to tap.

edges.label: Price per cubic metre
edges.detail: Higher prices pay for the new plants and nudge use down.

edges.label: Rainwater run-off
edges.detail: Drains and canals steer rain into reservoirs.

edges.label: Up to 250 million gallons a day
edges.detail: Raw river water, under the 1962 agreement.

edges.label: Seawater
edges.detail: Pumped in and pushed through membranes.

edges.label: Used water from homes and industry
Used water, by gravity
edges.detail: Cleaned first at the reclamation plants.

edges.label: Added to reservoirs in dry periods
edges.detail: NEWater is added to reservoirs when rain runs short.

edges.label: Ultra-pure water
edges.detail: Cleaner than tap water, which chipmaking needs.

edges.label: Drinking water
edges.detail: Joins the same pipes as reservoir water.

edges.label: Treated water, sold back
edges.detail: Johor may buy up to 2% of what Singapore draws.

edges.label: Samples from the network
edges.detail: Checked against standards based on WHO guidelines.

phases.label: Now
phases.detail: Finish the tunnels, price water at its cost.

phases.label: By 2060
phases.detail: Grow the taps that don't depend on rain or Johor.

plan.label: Finish the deep tunnel system, phase 2
plan.detail: Phase 2 was about 80% complete at 30 November 2025.

plan.label: Open Tuas Water Reclamation Plant
plan.detail: Treats 650,000 cubic metres of used water from homes and 150,000 from industry a day.
needs: Finish the deep tunnel system, phase 2

plan.label: Price water at its cost
plan.detail: Up 20 cents a cubic metre in 2024 and 30 more in 2025.

plan.label: Grow NEWater to 55%
plan.detail: More reclaimed water, mostly for industry.

plan.label: Grow desalination to 30%
plan.detail: A sixth plant is being studied.

plan.label: Meet demand without Johor
plan.detail: When the 1962 agreement ends, local sources must meet all demand.
